youtube.title: A New York Judge Destroyed His Files, Then Vanished Forever | Judge Crater
youtube.description:
On 6 August 1930, New York Supreme Court Justice Joseph Force Crater, appointed four months earlier by Governor Franklin Roosevelt, spent the morning going through his files and reportedly destroying documents. His clerk cashed two checks totaling $5,150, and the two carried two locked briefcases to his apartment; the briefcases were never found. That evening he dined at Billy Haas's chophouse on West 45th Street with a friend and a showgirl, held a reserved seat for a Broadway show, said goodbye outside the restaurant, and was never seen again. The alarm was not raised for almost four weeks. The press called him the "missingest man in America." He was declared legally dead in 1939. In 2005, a note left by a widow claimed a police officer had killed him and buried him at Coney Island; nothing was ever found.

📂 Case File #031: Judge Crater
